interpretation: What the restriction concedes: about health not every woman, child or beast is competent to heal itself (171e); about what is advantageous one counsellor differs from another, and one city's opinion from another's, toward truth (πρὸς ἀλήθειαν), and no one would dare say that what a city thinks advantageous will in every case be so (172a). Read weakly: outside the domain something seems so to someone without being true for them. One strengthening is stated: that one judgement differs from another toward truth is read as an actual case of seeming without truth-for (a worse judgement), not merely as its possibility. Not read as an explicit endorsement of absolute truth; the bridge from "not made true by seeming" to absolute truth is open.
